headline: erad raises $22m Series A led by MEVP
summary: The Riyadh-based Shariah-compliant SME lender is expanding across the GCC, including the UAE.
points: The round was led by MEVP; erad's Saudi business grew eightfold in a year.
It has financed over SAR 500m and received more than SAR 4bn of funding applications.
New products target capital-heavy sectors such as industry, logistics and manufacturing.
MEVP describes the GCC SME financing gap as about $250bn.
why: A well-funded regional lender moving into the UAE; it competes for SME clients, though not yet in healthcare claims.

headline: ADGM's Numou marketplace nears 1,000 SMEs and AED 200m of requests
summary: Abu Dhabi's SME financing marketplace lets businesses compare offers from banks, fintechs and government programmes.
points: Numou has close to 1,000 registered SMEs, which have requested more than AED 200m of financing.
17 financing partners offer over 40 products, including receivables lender Zelo, invoice financier Abhi and revenue-based lender FlapKap.
It pulls in bank statements, contracts, purchase orders and invoices so lenders see a fuller picture of each applicant.
A bank-account journey is planned as the next phase.
why: A distribution channel, not just a rival: Factor could join Numou as a financing partner to reach Abu Dhabi clinics.

headline: Beehive takes a majority stake in Saudi crowdfunding platform Thimar
summary: The Dubai SME lending marketplace, part of e&, bought control of a licensed Saudi debt crowdfunding platform.
points: Beehive Group Holdings acquired a majority of Thimar; the stake size was not disclosed.
Thimar gives Beehive a fully regulated platform in Saudi Arabia.
Beehive entered Saudi Arabia in 2020 through bank partnerships and has financed more than 3,000 SMEs across the GCC.
why: Established UAE players are buying their way into Saudi Arabia; Factor's own GCC expansion may face the same licensing route.

headline: Klaim secures up to $25m private credit facility
summary: The healthcare claims financier added debt capacity to fund more advances to providers.
points: The facility of up to $25m is from an undisclosed private credit lender.
It funds Klaim's Accelerate product, which advances cash to providers against eligible insurance receivables.
Klaim did not disclose provider numbers, receivables volume or revenue.
why: Klaim is building the same funding stack Factor needs; its lender is a likely target for Factor's own warehouse line.

headline: Claritev invests $2m in Klaim to grow in the US and MENA
summary: The strategic investment supports Klaim's provider-payment platform in both regions.
points: Claritev committed $2m and joins existing partners VMG and Ascend BPO.
Klaim now describes itself as a healthcare revenue treasury platform: forecasting, accelerating and recovering cash from insurance receivables.
It runs klaim.com in the US and klaim.ai in the Middle East.
why: Klaim is moving beyond funding into software for clinics' revenue cycle; Factor's AI-led screening needs a clear edge on price or speed.

headline: Yango Group makes its first MENA investment in Comfi
summary: Yango's venture arm joined Comfi's pre-Series A round; the amount was not stated.
points: Comfi offers B2B buy-now-pay-later, invoice discounting and dealer financing embedded in suppliers' workflows.
It serves more than 1,000 SMEs and has processed over 15,000 invoices.
Yango says it backs startups building digital infrastructure in emerging markets.
why: Comfi is the best-funded UAE invoice discounter; it does not target healthcare claims today.

headline: Comfi raises $65m pre-Series A in equity and debt
summary: The Dubai embedded-finance startup will scale underwriting and expand across MENA and the GCC.
points: Iliad Partners led the equity, with Yango Ventures and Raw Ventures joining.
Partners for Growth provided a credit facility and Shorooq structured a mezzanine facility.
Comfi reports over 1,000 clients and 15,000 invoices processed since its 2023 founding.
The equity and debt split was not disclosed.
why: Shows how much capital UAE invoice finance can attract; a benchmark for Factor's own raise and debt structure.

headline: Fincobox widens its SME liquidity products in Dubai
summary: The firm offers invoice discounting of up to 90% within a day, alongside other short-term finance.
points: Products include invoice discounting, revenue-based finance, purchase-order finance and short-term facilities.
It targets SMEs that banks reject for lack of collateral or slow approvals.
why: Competes on speed for general SME invoices; not focused on insurer-backed claims.

headline: Klaim raises $26m to speed up insurance claim payments for providers
summary: The Dubai healthcare fintech raised $10m of equity and $16m of debt to grow in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Oman.
points: Saudi investor Mad'a led the equity, with Morocco's CDG Invest participating.
A SAR 60m healthcare financing fund with Tharawat Tuwaiq backs its Saudi expansion.
Klaim pays providers within 24 hours of claim submission, against typical insurer cycles of 60 to 90 days.
It is moving up-market to hospital groups and larger provider networks.
why: Klaim is Factor's closest competitor: same product, same clients, same insurers. Factor needs a clear reason for clinics to switch.

headline: Aura Finance plugs invoice financing into Wafeq's accounting software
summary: UAE SMEs using Wafeq can fund unpaid invoices through Aura without leaving their accounting tool.
points: Invoices sync from Wafeq; the SME picks which to fund and submits.
Aura advertises advances of up to 95% of invoice value, with funds in about one business day.
The SME repays Aura directly; the figures are the companies' own claims.
why: Embedding finance in software clinics already use is a channel Factor should copy, for example via clinic billing systems.

headline: J.P. Morgan backs Saudi lender Lendo with a $690m warehouse facility
summary: The SAR 2.6bn facility lets Lendo scale SME lending and launch new products in Saudi Arabia.
points: J.P. Morgan led the warehouse facility, one of the largest for a GCC fintech.
Lendo previously raised a $28m Series B led by Sanabil, part of Saudi Arabia's PIF.
It fits Saudi Arabia's goal of lifting SME lending to 20% of financing by 2030.
why: Global banks will fund GCC receivables books at scale once a track record exists; a model for Factor's later funding.

headline: Emirates Development Bank and Klaim launch healthcare receivables financing
summary: The state development bank teamed up with Klaim to fund insurance claims for UAE providers of all sizes.
points: Klaim buys claims from providers, collects from insurers and runs the process end to end.
Providers can be paid within 24 hours instead of waiting 60 to 90 days.
EDB put UAE annual healthcare claims at about AED 22bn, with AED 5.5bn unsettled at any time.
why: Klaim has government-backed funding behind it; Factor could seek a similar EDB arrangement.
